# Examples

## `profiles.toml`

[`profiles.toml`](profiles.toml) shows the profile file format.

## What GitMate writes

`gitmate rules add ~/work work` appends one section to your global Git
config (shown with the absolute paths it writes):

```ini
[includeIf "gitdir:/home/ada/work/"]
	path = /home/ada/.config/gitmate/includes/work.gitconfig
```

and keeps the generated include file in sync with the profile:

```ini
# Generated by GitMate from profiles.toml. Changes here are overwritten.
[user]
	name = Ada Lovelace
	email = ada@acme.example
[core]
	sshCommand = ssh -i '/home/ada/.ssh/id_ed25519_acme' -o IdentitiesOnly=yes
```

(`core.sshCommand` is only present when the profile has an SSH key.)

`gitmate use work` in a repository writes to that repository's
`.git/config`:

```ini
[user]
	name = Ada Lovelace
	email = ada@acme.example
```

and with `--ssh` also:

```ini
[core]
	sshCommand = ssh -i '/home/ada/.ssh/id_ed25519_acme' -o IdentitiesOnly=yes
```

Each of these is shown as a preview first and can be reversed with
`gitmate undo`.
